title: POC: Latency vs Cost — Hybrid-Precision Roadtest and Prompt Warmup
content:
Context: FinServ-X POC (sensitive docs). Goal: demonstrate 200ms tail latency for short QA/IR queries (avg input 128 tokens) while keeping token cost < $0.0009/resp. Private deployment (VPC) with 2x A100 40GB nodes; customer will move to Dedicated after POC.

Quick summary of experiments run (notes and rough numbers)
- Model candidates: Llama-2-13B-chat (FP16), Mistral-7B-v0 (FP16), Llama-2-13B (4-bit QAT down to int4, adaptive block quant), Falcon-40B-instruct (quantized to 5-bit), MosaicTiny-reranker (small reranker for cascade)
- Baseline (no quant, no KV cache): Llama-2-13B on single A100: p50=110ms, p95=480ms, tokens/sec ~65, cost est $0.0022/resp -> fails cost SLO
- KV prefix caching enabled (per-conversation): p50=95ms, p95=320ms, tokens/sec ~80, cost drop ~12%
- Mixed precision + int4 adaptive block quant (applied to feed-forward only, keep softmax FP16): p50=70ms, p95=210ms, tokens/sec ~120, quality-drop measured by Eval set BLEU/EM small (~1.6% delta)
- Hybrid routing: small-model-first cascade (Mistral-7B for easy queries; offload to quant-13B on low confidence): hit-rate 62% on small model, overall p95 190ms, cost est $0.00072/resp -> meets cost target with marginal quality loss
- Reranker: MosaicTiny scoring top-5 outputs from small model before invoking large model reduced false fallback by ~14% and improved downstream accuracy for top chosen responses

Key observations
- Quantization strategy matters: full-int4 across all layers introduced hallucination in certain legal-style prompts. Adaptive block quant with FP16 for attention and softmax maintained fidelity while saving memory.
- KV cache warmup: prompt warmup (sending model synthetic prefix tokens before real traffic) reduced p95 by ~30ms in steady-state due to warmed KV allocations in the runtime. For private deployments we scripted a prewarming flow in rollout pipeline.
- Batch sizing: Continuous batching helps throughput but increases p95 for single-user latency. For SLOs, use dynamic latency-first allocator: prefer single-request fast-path for interactive routes, allow batching for high-throughput background routes.
- Fallback policy: when GPU pool utilization >85%, route to dedicated smaller quant variant instead of failing. Implemented a detection window 15s with smoothing to avoid flip-flops.

Quality checks and evals
- Prompt set: 180 prompts sampled from customer transcripts + 40 adversarial legal edge cases. We ran automated evals comparing baseline FP16 to hybrid-int4 variant. Metrics: ROUGE, EM, hallucination checklist (manual for 40 cases).
- Thresholds: allow up to 2% drop in EM for responses where latency meets SLO; anything >2% requires roll-forward to FP16 path.

Operational notes (runbook fragments)
- Deployment steps: 1) Provision 2x A100 nodes in customer VPC 2) Install private control plane agent 3) Upload quantized model artifacts (digest + signature) 4) Seed warmup cache for top 100 active conversations 5) Flip traffic with canary 5% -> 25% -> 100%
- Monitoring: Surface per-model p50/p95, routing hit-rate, cascade fallback count, and per-route token cost. Alert if p95 > 240ms or fallback rate > 18%.

Open questions / TODOs
- Quant training: should we run a small QAT pass on customer-specific data (redacted) to reduce hallucination on legal phrasing? (JIRA-ENG-2230)
- Can we reduce prewarm overhead by delta-compressed cache snapshots? Investigate KV snapshotting in runtime (GH issue #821)
- Cost model fine-tune: include network egress and storage in final estimate for customer contract

Next steps / Recommendations for customer
1) Proceed with hybrid-precision variant + cascade for proof-of-concept. Merchant risk acceptable given evals.
2) Run 24h production shadow traffic with live transcripts to validate hallucination risk and fallback behavior.
3) Budget a brief QAT step focused on 6k annotated legal QA pairs to bring EM delta <1% if customer approves.

Appendix (links and quick commands)
- Quick run: ./scripts/deploy_poc --env vpc-finserv-x --models hybrid-13b-int4 --warmup 100
- Perf dashboard (internal): https://observability.redwood.ai/dashboards/poc-finserv-x
- Related PRs / notes: see linked artifacts above

Notes to self: keep the customer privacy redactions in shared docs. Flag the 40 failed edge-case prompts in the next workshop with SE and legal.
